subject.title: feat: provider fallback by failure class — quarantine auth-broken providers

question: Which auth-failure signals should become default provider/profile quarantine versus transient same-key retry or the existing opt-in skip behavior?
rationale: The remaining work changes provider routing defaults, status visibility, and auth-state side effects for existing users, and current policy deliberately keeps some auth-looking failures recoverable to avoid false lockouts.

options.title: Approve conservative default quarantine
options.body: Classify only high-confidence revoked/invalidated credential and confirmed refresh failures into the disabled/quarantine lane, retry same-key transient 401s once first, and expose redacted status/doctor recovery state.

options.title: Keep skip behavior opt-in
options.body: Leave current default retries unchanged and rely on `OPENCLAW_FALLBACK_SKIP_TTL_MS` plus existing `auth_permanent` handling for operators who want faster avoidance of known-bad candidates.

options.title: Split status and restart first
options.body: Handle provider-health status and the single-key restart loop in a narrower issue before changing fallback routing defaults.

recommendation.title: Approve conservative default quarantine
recommendation.body: Classify only high-confidence revoked/invalidated credential and confirmed refresh failures into the disabled/quarantine lane, retry same-key transient 401s once first, and expose redacted status/doctor recovery state.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is an upgrade-sensitive provider-routing and gateway-lifecycle policy decision, and Peter has the strongest adjacent architecture history in these files.
